paper_metadata.title: Harnessing ordered-disordered phase synergy for enhanced high-temperature strength in refractory high-entropy alloys

The optimized composition, (Al,Cr)0.6Mo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr, achieves a comparatively outstanding compressive yield strength of 665.61 MPa and a compressive peak strength of 730.35 MPa at 1000 C — representing a 75.43 % and 80.73 % enhancement, respectively, compared to the baseline Mo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr alloy.

The optimized composition, (Al,Cr)0.6Mo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr, achieves a comparatively outstanding compressive yield strength of 665.61 MPa and a compressive peak strength of 730.35 MPa at 1000 C — representing a 75.43 % and 80.73 % enhancement, respectively, compared to the baseline Mo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr alloy.

Strengthening arises from synergistic second-phase precipitation, grain refinement, solid-solution effects, and dislocation impediment, while the adverse impact of ordering on room-temperature plasticity is mitigated at high temperatures via thermal activation and cross-slip of screw dislocations.
